**Bottom line:** the course labs run on your own Windows 11 PC or Mac. You install one free program (Docker Desktop),
unzip the course labs file, double-click **Start Course Labs**, and press **Start** next to a lab. Your work stays on
your computer. You can do it at home before class.

You need:

- **A Windows 11 PC or a Mac.** This page shows both.
- **About 8 GB of memory.** Docker Desktop on Windows lists 8 GB of system memory [@docker_windowsinstall_2026]; on a
  Mac it lists 4 GB [@docker_macinstall_2026]. The labs themselves are light: the biggest (Bitcoin) held
  about 1.7 GB while running, the Fabric lab about 1 GB, and most under 1 GB. The control page tells you if Docker has too
  little. Docker's figures are as of 9 Nov 2026; the lab figures were measured on 10 Nov 2026 on a 16 GB Windows 11 PC.
- **An internet connection and disk space.** Each lab downloads once, the first time you press
  **Start**. Downloads run from about 35 MB to about 830 MB per lab (the Fabric lab downloads about 1.3 GB in all), as
  measured on 10 Nov 2026. Unpacked on disk the labs take several times that: all sixteen together can take up to about 40 GB (the
  sum of the images' unpacked sizes on 10 Nov 2026; layers they share are stored once, so it is usually less), so keep 40 GB
  free if you plan to use them all. The control page shows each lab's size before you start.
- **Permission to install software.** On a work computer, ask your IT staff to install Docker Desktop for you if you
  cannot.

## Get the course labs {#get-the-labs}

1. Download [**Course-Labs.zip**](https://github.com/astevegreen/blockchain-technology-course/releases/latest/download/Course-Labs.zip).
   The course home page links the same file; it is the latest course labs release on the course's GitHub page.
2. **Windows:** right-click the zip and choose **Extract All**, then **Extract**. Do not run anything from inside the
   zip; work from the extracted folder.
3. **Mac:** double-click the zip. A folder appears next to it.
4. Open the new folder. You will see **Start Course Labs**, **Stop Course Labs** and **READ-ME-FIRST**.

## Install Docker Desktop {#install-docker}

Docker Desktop is the program that runs the labs. Install it once. If it is already on your computer, skip to
[the first launch](#first-launch).

### Windows 11

1. Go to [docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/windows-install](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/windows-install/)
   and press the **Docker Desktop for Windows - x86_64** download button. (On an Arm PC, use the **Docker Desktop for Windows - Arm (Early Access)**
   download listed beside it.)
2. Double-click **Docker Desktop Installer.exe**.
3. If a box offers **Use WSL 2 instead of Hyper-V**, leave it ticked [@docker_windowsinstall_2026].
4. Follow the installer's prompts and wait for it to finish.
5. If the installer asks you to restart, restart the computer.
6. Open Docker Desktop from the Start menu. It does not start by itself after installing
   [@docker_windowsinstall_2026].
7. Accept the terms if Docker asks.
8. Wait until Docker Desktop says it is running. This takes a minute or two.

Windows 11 needs version 23H2 or newer (Pro, Enterprise or Education), and Docker needs the WSL 2 feature, version 2.1.5 or later
[@docker_windowsinstall_2026] (as of 9 Nov 2026). Press the Windows key, type **winver** and press Enter to see your
version. Docker's list names Pro, Enterprise and Education; the same page says Home editions run Linux containers, which
is all the labs use [@docker_windowsinstall_2026]. If Docker refuses to install on Windows 11 Home, tell your instructor.

### Mac

1. Go to [docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/mac-install](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/mac-install/).
2. Pick the download that matches your Mac: **Apple silicon** (M1 or newer) or **Intel chip**. To check, choose
   **Apple menu**, then **About This Mac**, and read the **Chip** line.
3. Double-click **Docker.dmg**, then drag the Docker icon onto **Applications**.
4. Double-click **Docker** in **Applications**.
5. Press **Accept** on Docker's terms. If your Mac asks for your login password to finish setting up, type it.
6. Wait until Docker Desktop says it is running.

Docker supports the current and the two previous major macOS releases [@docker_macinstall_2026] (as of 9 Nov 2026).

## Start the labs for the first time {#first-launch}

Your computer has never seen **Start Course Labs** before, so it warns you. The course labs are not signed with a
paid certificate, which is why the warning appears. Open the file only from the course zip you downloaded from the
link above. The steps below let it run once.

### Windows 11

1. In the folder, double-click **Start Course Labs** (it may show as `Start-Course-Labs.cmd`).
2. A blue box says **Windows protected your PC**. This is Microsoft Defender SmartScreen warning about a file it does
   not recognise [@microsoft_smartscreen_2026].
3. Press **More info**.
4. Press **Run anyway**.
5. A black window opens. If Docker Desktop is closed, it starts Docker Desktop and says "Starting Docker Desktop.
   This can take a minute..."
6. The first time, it says "Getting the latest course labs. The first time takes a few minutes..." Wait.
7. Your browser opens the control page. You can close the black window once the page has opened.

If the box has no **More info** link, or no **Run anyway** button, your organisation has blocked the file. Ask your IT
staff to allow it.

### Mac

1. In the folder, double-click **Start Course Labs**.
2. macOS says it cannot verify the file and does not open it. Press **Done**. This is expected.
3. Choose **Apple menu**, then **System Settings**, then **Privacy & Security** in the sidebar. Scroll down to
   **Security**.
4. Press **Open Anyway** next to the message about Start Course Labs. The button is there for about an hour after the
   first attempt [@apple_openunknowndeveloper_2026].
5. Type your Mac login password and press **OK**.
6. Press **Open** if macOS asks once more. After this, double-clicking works normally
   [@apple_openunknowndeveloper_2026].
7. A Terminal window opens and prints what it is doing. Your browser then opens the control page.

Apple's own page shows each of these screens with pictures: [Open a Mac app from an unknown developer](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/open-a-mac-app-from-an-unknown-developer-mh40616/mac)
[@apple_openunknowndeveloper_2026].

The steps are the same on later visits, minus the warning: double-click **Start Course Labs**.

### If you use Linux

Run `Start-Course-Labs.sh` from a terminal. Everything after this works as described.

## The control page {#control-page}

The page is at **http://127.0.0.1:8470/**. It only exists on your own computer, and nobody else can see it. Bookmark
it. It works only while the labs are started.

![The control page of course labs release 2026.11.10-11 on a Windows 11 PC, after a few labs were tried. Each lab is a card: a title, the course day, the memory it needs, a state, and buttons. Here two labs are running and the others are stopped. The memory figures shown are that release's estimates; later releases show measured ones.](assets/run-labs/control-labs.png){fig-alt="The Course Labs control page listing the labs as cards. Tron Lab and Cross-Chain Lab say Running, with Open, Stop and Reset buttons. The others say Stopped (your work is kept), with Start and Reset buttons."}

### What each state means

| The card says | What it means | What you can do |
|---|---|---|
| Not downloaded yet | The lab is not on your computer yet. The card shows its download size. | Press **Start**. It downloads, then starts. |
| Ready to start | Downloaded, not running. | Press **Start**. |
| Starting | Downloading or getting ready. A bar shows progress. | Wait and leave the page open. A big first download can take a long while on a slow connection. |
| Running | The lab works. | Press **Open**. |
| Stopped (your work is kept) | You stopped it. Your work is saved. | Press **Start** to carry on. |
| Didn't start | Something went wrong. The card says what, in plain words. | Do what the card says, then press **Start** again. [More in Troubleshooting](#trouble). |
| Not available on this computer | The lab does not run on your computer's processor. | Nothing. The card says why. |

### What each button does

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Start** | Downloads the lab if needed, then starts it. |
| **Open** | Opens the lab in a new browser tab at an address starting `http://127.0.0.1`. |
| **Stop** | Stops that lab and keeps your work. |
| **Reset** | Puts that lab back to how it was at the start of the course. It first asks "Reset this lab?" Press **Keep my work** to cancel, or **Reset** to delete everything you did in that lab. |
| **Load the forensics chain** | Only on the **Bitcoin Lab**. It loads the case you will investigate. It takes a few minutes, and the card says "Leave this page open". The lab is not ready for the exercise until it finishes. |

**Reset deletes your work in that lab and cannot be undone.** Use **Stop**, not **Reset**, when you only want to finish
for the day.

Open **About this computer** at the bottom of the page to see whether Docker is running, how much memory Docker has,
your processor, whether you are online, and which ports other programs are using.

### The Fabric lab

The **Hyperledger Fabric Lab** (day 5) works like the others, with one difference. The first **Start** takes longer
because it downloads about 760 MB of Fabric programs and images the first time; the card's download bar does not show that part. It needs Docker Desktop 4.29 or newer, the first version that
ships Docker Engine 26 [@docker_desktop429_2024] (as of 9 Nov 2026). If your Docker is older, the lab's card says so; see [If something goes wrong](#trouble).

### When the page says "A newer version of the course labs is out"

Do the **Stop** steps below, then double-click **Start Course Labs** again. Your work is kept.

## Stop the labs {#stop}

When you finish for the day:

1. Close the lab tabs in your browser.
2. In the course labs folder, double-click **Stop Course Labs**.
3. Wait for "The course labs are stopped. Double-click Start Course Labs to carry on later."

Your work is kept. You do not need to quit Docker Desktop, but you can. Next time, double-click **Start Course Labs**.
The warning from your computer appears only the first time.

If you shut the computer down without pressing **Stop Course Labs**, nothing is lost. Docker Desktop may start the
labs again by itself when it opens; press **Stop Course Labs** when you finish.

## If something goes wrong {#trouble}

The messages below are the ones the launcher shows (some end differently depending on your computer). Find yours, then try the fix.

![The notice the control page shows when it opens and cannot reach Docker. Taken on a Windows 11 PC from the launcher's source with release 2026.11.10-11's lab list, and Docker's address pointed at nothing. Release 2026.11.10-11 itself shows this notice only after you press Start; later releases show it as soon as the page opens.](assets/run-labs/control-docker-down.png){fig-alt="The control page with a yellow notice: Docker isn't running. Open Docker Desktop, wait until it says it is running, then reload this page."}

| What you see | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Docker Desktop isn't installed. The guide that just opened shows how to install it." | [Install Docker Desktop](#install-docker), then double-click **Start Course Labs** again. |
| "Docker didn't start. Open Docker Desktop yourself, wait until it says it is running, then try again." | Open Docker Desktop from the Start menu (Windows) or Applications (Mac). Wait until it says it is running. Run **Start Course Labs** again. On Windows, if Docker complains that virtualization is off, ask IT to turn on hardware virtualization in the computer's BIOS or UEFI settings [@docker_windowsinstall_2026]. |
| "Couldn't download the course labs. Check your internet connection, then try again." | Connect to the internet. On a work network, ask IT to allow downloads from `ghcr.io`. |
| "The course labs didn't start. Restart Docker Desktop, then try again." or "The labs page didn't start." | Quit Docker Desktop, open it again, wait until it says it is running, then double-click **Start Course Labs**. |
| "Docker isn't running. Open Docker Desktop, wait until it says it is running, then reload this page." | Open Docker Desktop, wait, then reload the page (press F5). |
| "The control page lost touch with Docker." | If you just pressed **Stop Course Labs**, this is expected. Otherwise double-click **Start Course Labs** again. |
| "Port 8443 is busy: another program on this computer is using it." (the number varies) | Close the other program, or restart the computer. Press **Start** again. **About this computer** lists the busy ports. |
| "Docker has 8 GB of memory but this lab needs 10 GB." (the numbers vary) | In Docker Desktop choose **Settings**, then **Resources**, and raise **Memory** to what the message says. Press **Apply**. On Windows the Memory setting may not be shown; if it is missing, tell your instructor. Then press **Start** again. |
| "This lab isn't available for this computer's processor." | Nothing is wrong with your computer. Use another lab, or ask your instructor how to do that exercise. |
| "No internet connection." | Connect to the internet and press **Start** again. |
| "Your computer is out of disk space for this lab." | Free some disk space, then press **Start** again. Labs you have finished can be cleared with **Reset** (it deletes your work in that lab). |
| "This lab's download isn't available yet." | Tell your instructor. The course files may not be published yet. |
| "Docker Desktop's Enhanced Container Isolation setting is blocking the labs." | Your organisation's Docker administrator set this. Ask them to turn it off for your computer. |
| "This computer is already running the course labs another way (the classroom setup)." | Stop those labs first, close the page, and double-click **Start Course Labs** again. |
| "This lab needs Docker Desktop 4.29 or newer. Update Docker Desktop, then press Start again." (the Fabric lab) | Update Docker Desktop from its own menu, or download it again from the [install page](#install-docker) and install over the old one. Then press **Start** again. |
| "Something went wrong while …" | Press **Start** to try again. If it happens again, tell your instructor. |
| "Docker isn't installed, so no labs are running." or "Docker isn't running, so no labs are running." (from **Stop Course Labs**) | Nothing to do: there was nothing to stop. |
| A lab will not start and the message is unclear | Press **Reset** on that lab and then **Start**. Reset deletes your work in that lab. |

Still stuck? Tell your instructor which message you saw and your computer type (Windows or Mac, and Intel, AMD or
Apple chip).
